headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from Chatwoot customer data flowing into a writable, networked RAG agent with secrets handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and interaction history, which can contain attacker-controlled text. The course agent reads files, runs subprocesses, and exposes API endpoints for agentic/RAG workflows, so if Chatwoot output is fed into it, prompt injection is plausible. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation content is passed into the course agent's /api/v1/ask or /api/v1/agentic-ask flow
IF the course agent treats retrieved text as instructions rather than untrusted content
mitigations: Add a system prompt that labels all Chatwoot text as untrusted input
Strip HTML/markdown and instruction-like phrases before passing content onward
Require human review for any action derived from customer messages
Log and flag prompt-injection markers in inbound Chatwoot content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Chatwoot and the RAG pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem. If they share a workspace or the course agent ingests Chatwoot exports, sensitive data could be copied into a system that also processes secrets and networked API calls. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports or transcripts are stored in the same local workspace as the course agent
IF the course agent uploads those files or derived context to external APIs
mitigations: Move Chatwoot exports to a separate directory with restricted permissions
Redact customer identifiers before ingestion
Disable automatic file pickup from shared folders
Review outbound API destinations for any prompt or file forwarding
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents in separate containers or VMs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and the course agent can execute shells, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even without git writes, both can mutate shared local resources or external services, creating overlapping write authority. Because shared-state behavior is not stated, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same working directory or Docker volume
IF either agent writes artifacts that the other later consumes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories and volumes
Run only one writer at a time during setup
Make generated artifacts read-only after creation
Check for accidental overwrites in shared config files
requires-engineering: add explicit locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints that may act on retrieved content. If Chatwoot output is forwarded into the course agent without verification, the second agent can amplify mistakes into downstream answers or actions. The absence of documented verification keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is used as retrieval context for the course agent
IF the course agent emits responses or actions without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations back to source records for generated claims
Limit the course agent to draft-only mode
Sample outputs for manual QA before release
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment with external API calls. If customer records or regulated support content are moved into the course agent, retention and residency controls may diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so the risk is compliance-process mismatch rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated customer support records are exported from Chatwoot into the course agent environment
IF the course agent's logging or external API calls retain that data beyond Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Classify which Chatwoot fields may enter the course agent
Disable retention of imported customer records in logs
Review data residency for any external API used by the course agent
Keep support data out of training or analytics stores
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
